name: LM4030AMF-2.5_NOPB
title: SOT-23 precision shunt voltage reference, 2.5 V and 4.096 V
summary: The LM4030 is a two-terminal shunt reference in a 5-pin SOT-23 at 2.5 V or 4.096 V. The A grade holds 0.05 % at 25 °C and 10 ppm/°C from 0 °C to 85 °C; B and C grades are 0.10 % and 0.15 %. It needs 120 µA (2.5 V) or 130 µA (4.096 V) at most, sinks up to 30 mA, and is stable with no capacitor or up to 10 µF. Thermal hysteresis is 75 ppm and 1000-hour drift 40 ppm, typical.
key_figures: 10 ppm/°C max, 0 to 85 °C (A); 20 to 30 ppm/°C max, -40 to 125 °C

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: A shunt reference fed from VIN through one resistor. RZ sets the current into the VREF node, which must cover the largest load current plus the reference's own minimum operating current; the LM4030 sinks whatever the load does not take and holds VREF. COUT is optional: the part is stable with none or with up to 10 µF, and a capacitor lowers the impedance at high frequency and the step in VREF when the load changes.

where.IMIN_OPERATING: minimum operating current of the reference

where.VREF1: output at 25 °C before the temperature excursion

where.ΔT: width of the operating temperature range

equations.name: Maximum power dissipation
equations.note: Capped at the 350 mW absolute maximum.

operation.text: A two-terminal shunt reference in SOT-23, fixed at 2.5 V or 4.096 V. It runs from 120 µA (2.5 V) or 130 µA (4.096 V) at most and sinks up to 30 mA continuously, 50 mA for under a second. No output capacitor is required; any value up to 10 µF can be fitted.
Three grades: A holds 0.05 % initial accuracy with a 10 ppm/°C limit from 0 °C to 85 °C and 20 ppm/°C over -40 °C to 125 °C; B holds 0.10 % and 20 ppm/°C; C holds 0.15 % and 30 ppm/°C.

The series resistor fixes the total current available at VREF. It has to pass the largest load current plus the reference's minimum operating current, so the reference always keeps enough to regulate. More current through the reference lowers its dynamic impedance, which falls roughly in inverse proportion to the shunt current, and so improves rejection of supply noise and EMI.

Stable with no capacitor or up to 10 µF. A capacitor improves load-transient response and broadband noise, and holds the impedance down at frequencies where the bare reference's impedance climbs. It goes as near to the part as possible so board parasitics and added ESR do not spoil the transient response.

Drift with time, thermal hysteresis and PCB-stress shifts in a reference come mostly from offsets between matched devices in its regulation loop. The LM4030 cancels these offsets dynamically, which gives 40 ppm typical long-term drift, 75 ppm typical hysteresis after eight -40 °C to 125 °C cycles, and low sensitivity to board stress in the SOT-23 package.
Drift is the spread between the highest and lowest output over the temperature range, divided by nominal output and range width (box method). The limit is 10 to 30 ppm/°C maximum by grade.

Change of VREF with current is small (25 ppm/mA typical on the 2.5 V option), so load swings up to 50 mA move it little. Resistance between the reference and its load adds a drop proportional to load current: place the LM4030 as near the load as possible. RZ can sit anywhere; COUT belongs right at the reference.
ESD protection on chip is limited. Store with the leads shorted together or in conductive foam.
